Redwood to provide benchmark plan, workload sizing spreadsheet, and redaction script (Jordan) - by 2028-11-13
Amberfield to provide redacted eval set, data flow diagram, and list of approvers (Elena/Priya) - by 2028-11-14

action_items: Maya Chen - send SOC2, ISO summary, security whitepaper, and incident response runbook - due 2028-11-10
Jordan Patel - draft benchmark plan, workload sizing calc, cost estimate, SAML metadata and redaction scripts - due 2028-11-13

header:
Date: 2028-11-09T15:00-08:00
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Ruiz (CTO, Amberfield), Samir Khan (Head of Platform), Priya Desai (Security Lead)
Meeting purpose: POC scoping for security pilot - agree success criteria, workload sizing and benchmarks, timelines, and security/compliance requirements (SOC 2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs).
summary: Quick scoping call to align on pilot success metrics (latency p95, cost per 1k tokens, accuracy thresholds), workload sizing (chat volume, peak concurrency), benchmark plan (end-to-end vs token-only), timeline for pilot (2-6 weeks), and security/compliance asks (SOC 2, ISO certs, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS). Action items include Redwood sending SOC2/ISO docs, benchmark plan, and Amberfield providing data flows and HIPAA constraints.
topics: Introductions; Success criteria; Workload sizing and expected QPS; Benchmark methodology; Security/compliance (SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, data residency, KMS); Timeline and next steps; Action items and owners.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. Quick roll call — Maya from Redwood and Jordan our solutions engineer. Elena? 
[00:08] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Hi — Elena here. Sorry, had back-to-back with ops. Samir on my left —
[00:12] Samir Khan: Hey all, Samir. 
[00:15] Priya Desai: Priya here, security — sorry if I jump in with a lot of questions.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Totally expected, that's why we scheduled this. High level agenda: align success criteria for the POC, figure out sizing and the benchmark plan, and run through the security/compliance asks. We'll wrap with next steps. 
[00:30] Jordan Patel: I'll cover the benchmark plan and sizing, and then dive a bit into the private deployment / VPC options for your compliance needs. 
[01:02] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Goal for us is pretty simple — prove we can replace our interim QA assistant with Redwood for clinical triage chat. Need to see latency under 300ms p95 for the short prompts, cost in line with our budgets, and maintain accuracy on our clinical intent detection > 92%. Also HIPAA safe handling of PHI. 
[01:28] Maya Chen: Great, so success criteria we've heard: latency p95 <= 300ms, accuracy > 92% on your eval set, and unit cost target — what are you thinking there? 
[01:38] Samir Khan: Ballpark $0.25 per 1k tokens is our current internal target, but flexible if the latency is better. We're more worried about concurrency — peak clinic hours we could see 120 concurrent sessions. 
[01:52] Jordan Patel: Thanks. For the pilot we'll size for your peak concurrency and a steady baseline. We'll capture token distribution across sessions — short prompts, medium context, some longer EHR snippets. Our typical approach is simulated traffic using your sample prompts plus synthetic loads. 
[02:20] Priya Desai: Ok on concurrency — on the security side, two non-negotiables: SOC 2 Type II (or equivalent), and SSO via SAML/Okta integration. Also detailed audit logs for every API call (IP, user, timestamp, model used, response hash) retained for at least 90 days, ideally 1 year. 
[02:44] Maya Chen: Understood. We are SOC 2 Type II compliant — I'll send the cert, plus our ISO 27001 summary. We support SSO/SAML with Okta and have RBAC at per-route and per-team level. Audit logs are available and we can configure retention. Jordan — quick details on encryption/KMS? 
[03:03] Jordan Patel: We support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in Dedicated and Private modes. For hosted we encrypt at rest with provider-managed keys, but we can offer bring-your-own-key for Private. Note: audit logs in hosted include token-level metadata; PHI redaction is something we recommend doing client-side as an additional layer. 
[03:28] Priya Desai: Clarify hosted vs dedicated vs private for data residency — we need assurances that PHI never leaves our VPC for the pilot. 
[03:36] Jordan Patel: For Private deployment we run the inference runtime in your VPC or on-prem; that guarantees traffic and KV cache stays inside your network. For Dedicated (reserved capacity), data flows through Redwood but we can enable network peering and strict egress rules. For hosted, by default traffic goes through our control plane. We'll map options to your constraints in the doc. 
[04:05] Dr. Elena Ruiz: On benchmarks — what will you measure exactly? End-to-end latency? Token throughput? Cost per 1k? 
[04:12] Jordan Patel: All of the above. Our benchmark plan for the pilot: 1) functional correctness with your eval set (accuracy metrics), 2) synthetic load to measure p50/p95/p99 latencies end-to-end, 3) token-only throughput to assess cost and batching efficiency, and 4) KV/prefix cache hit rate impact. We'll provide a spreadsheet to capture assumptions. 
[04:46] Maya Chen: We'll also want to test fallback behavior — what happens when a model variant is overloaded. Jordan, can you include rollback/canary behavior in the plan? 
[04:55] Jordan Patel: Yep — we'll include routing policies and fallback to smaller/quantized variants, plus observed quality regression thresholds. 
[05:12] Samir Khan: For workload sizing, our rough numbers: average 10k sessions/day, peak 120 concurrent, average tokens per session 350, 95th percentile tokens 1,200. Will that be enough for you to size GPUs? 
[05:28] Jordan Patel: That gives a good starting point. For those numbers, if we run a quantized 16-bit and 4-bit mix we can talk about a fleet of 3-4 A100-equivalent GPUs for Dedicated, or a private cluster if you want on-prem. We'll run a sizing calc and include rough cost estimates. 
[05:52] Priya Desai: We also need RBAC mapping to our internal roles — dev, platform, security, and clinical ops. Need audit trails that show which role invoked which route. 
[06:03] Maya Chen: We support role mapping via SAML assertions and can map to RBAC in the console. Jordan, note to include per-route RBAC examples in the artifact. 
[06:18] Jordan Patel: Will do. Also to confirm: do you need model explainability outputs or token-level provenance for clinical decisions? 
[06:26] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Some explainability — at least to link responses to source snippets in the EHR, and an ability to flag hallucinations. Not full provenance yet but the pilot should surface those cases. 
[06:40] Jordan Patel: Ok we'll instrument the evals to capture hallucination rate and include annotations in the benchmark outputs. 
[07:01] Maya Chen: On timelines — what's your target to run the pilot? 
[07:05] Dr. Elena Ruiz: We'd like to start a week from today if possible, and run for 4 weeks, decision check after that. We have internal approvals but security needs to review the whitepaper. 
[07:18] Maya Chen: Tight but doable. We'll aim to have SOC2/ISO docs, benchmark plan, and a test account by EOD tomorrow. Jordan will draft workload sizing and cost estimates by Monday. 
[07:29] Priya Desai: Please include a clear data flow diagram showing where PHI resides and steps for redaction. Also we need SLA and incident response procedures. 
[07:38] Maya Chen: We'll attach our security whitepaper and incident response runbook. Link in chat: https://redwood.example/security-whitepaper.pdf (action: Maya to send official copies). 
[07:48] Samir Khan: For the benchmarks — we want both synthetic and a small subset of redacted real queries to run against a Private instance. How do we redaction for the test dataset? 
[07:58] Jordan Patel: We recommend a two-stage approach: 1) client-side redaction script to remove PHI and replace identifiers, 2) tokenization check to ensure no residual PII in payloads. We'll share a redaction script and notebook. 
[08:15] Dr. Elena Ruiz: On audit logs retention — you said 90 days default, we need up to 1 year. Is that configurable in Dedicated/Private? 
[08:23] Jordan Patel: In Private it's configurable to your retention policies; in Dedicated we can set longer retention via enterprise add-on. Hosted default is 90 days unless you purchase extended retention. We'll note pricing for that. 
[08:38] Priya Desai: SSO integration — we use Okta, SCIM for provisioning. Need groups sync and role mapping. 
[08:45] Maya Chen: Okta + SCIM is supported; SCIM for provisioning, and group sync for mapping to RBAC. Jordan will include sample SAML metadata and SCIM endpoints. 
[08:58] Samir Khan: Any constraints on KV cache persistence and encryption? If we have user chat sessions that cache context, we need TTLs and encryption. 
[09:05] Jordan Patel: KV cache can be persisted to encrypted storage with customer-managed keys in Private. TTLs are configurable per-workload. We'll include recommended settings for clinical workloads (short TTL, conservative caching). 
[09:28] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Do you have SOC 2 and ISO certificates we can share with procurement? 
[09:33] Maya Chen: Yes will send SOC 2 Type II and ISO summary. We'll add our third-party pen-test summary redacted as requested. 
[09:45] Priya Desai: For HIPAA we need BAAs for any PHI processing. Is Redwood willing to sign a BAA? 
[09:52] Maya Chen: Yes, we have a standard BAA for Private and Dedicated customers; for hosted we'll review scope but typically we can support BAAs in enterprise agreements. Legal will handle the specifics. 
[10:07] Jordan Patel: Anything else on the technical side — networking, peering, static IPs for egress, certs? 
[10:14] Samir Khan: We'll need static egress IPs for firewall allowlist during pilot. 
[10:18] Jordan Patel: Supported, we'll provide IP ranges and can set up a peering connection for Dedicated/Private. 
[10:25] Maya Chen: Ok let's recap next steps and owners — I'll list action items in the recap. 
[10:30] Maya Chen: Recap: Maya send SOC2/ISO and security whitepaper; Jordan send benchmark plan, workload sizing spreadsheet, redaction scripts, SAML metadata; Amberfield (Priya/Samir/Elena) to provide redacted eval set, data flow diagram, and list of approval contacts. Aim to start pilot 2028-11-16 for four weeks. 
[10:56] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Sounds good, thanks everyone. We'll review docs and get back on approvals. 
[11:02] Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links and schedule the kickoff. 
[11:06] End of recording (approx 52 minutes).
